title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
abstract: arXiv:2611.23219v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or access to real-world data. We find that sufficiently capable models do self-improve under these conditions, demonstrating strategies that align with classic cognitive frameworks for self-regulated learn

translated_title: 大语言模型智能体还需要被告知如何自我改进吗？
translated_abstract: 大语言模型智能体越来越多地驱动着自身的学习。自我改进方法将模型优化的各种组件委托给模型本身。随着模型能力的不断增强，这引出了一个基本问题：这些日益强大的模型是否仍需要我们来指定它们应如何自我改进？在本文中，我们研究了一种自主范式：在给定基本要素、资源和自我改进总体目标的情况下，智能体自行构建用于基于上下文优化的自学习算法。以游戏对局作为测试平台，一个冻结的大语言模型智能体被给予计算预算以及收集经验和更新文本文档的工具，并被允许在不受外部强加循环限制、也无法访问真实世界数据的条件下自由实验。我们发现，足够强大的模型在这些条件下确实能够实现自我改进，并展现出与经典自我调节学习认知框架相一致的策略。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种完全自主的自我改进范式，证明足够强大的冻结大语言模型智能体在仅有基本要素、工具和计算预算、且无人类指定方法或外部强加循环的条件下，能够自行构建自学习算法并实现自我改进，其策略与经典自我调节学习认知框架相符。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a fully autonomous self-improvement paradigm, demonstrating that sufficiently capable frozen LLM agents can construct their own learning algorithms and self-improve—without humans specifying how or imposing an external loop—given only basic primitives, tools, and a compute budget, with their strategies aligning with classic self-regulated learning frameworks.
